                      JAMES SALTER'S DAYS IN FILM

      James Salter was a pilot in the United States Air Force. He abandoned the military
       profession in 1957 after the publication of his first novel, The Hunters. He is best
     known as a novelist, but during the sixties and seventies, he worked in film making.
       Salter made documentaries, wrote scripts for films, and even was the director of a film
       called Three, starring Charlotte Rampling and Sam Waterston.

      Burning the Days, a short story published in The New Yorker in 1997, where Salter
        tells the story of his life, was adapted into a film called Passionate Falsehoods.

       Salter's time in the film world is both good and bad. In Rome, he met directors and
        stars. In New York, he explored the city with Robert Redford and enjoyed being famous.
      Deborah Treisman, and Michael Agger have talked about Salter. Nick Paumgarten in
     The Last Book, describes Salter's opinion about his film career:

      "Of sixteen scripts for movies, only four were popular. There was money, attractive
     women, and entrance into rooms where there were stories more for the dinner table
      than for the page". Salter thought he was wasting his time.

      Perhaps he wasted his time in a larger artistic way, but it still makes for attractive
       reading. The Last Book is available to everyone in online stores.
